title: I turned technical setups into smells and hooked a up fly's brain to trade stocks
author: IndependentBid6893
selftext:
I turned asset’s technical setup into a smell matrix and feed that into a digital twin of a fruit fly's smell circuit. It then buys its favorite and takes profit on the smell of these assets alone.

Six standard readings, such as RSI and volume against its average, are spread across the fly's 51 smell channels. It never sees a ticker, so what it learns on one company applies to any other with similar setups. 

The wiring is a complete map of one fruit fly's nervous system, about 166,000 neurons, published in 2025.   
  
The system simulates the 7,443 that handle smell. Each smell lights about 2% of its 4,064 learning cells, and which ones light is the fly's opinion.

It then learns from winning and losing trades. being more attracted to smells that made it money, and less from to smells that lost it money.

[https://www.clawstreet.io/fly?fly=fly2](https://www.clawstreet.io/fly?fly=fly2)

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: first trading bot I've seen with an actual nose. with six readings spread over 51 channels I'd want to see it next to a plain logistic regression on the same six inputs before giving the fly credit, a lot of fancy models turn out to be that regression in a costume.

replies.author: IndependentBid6893
replies.body: I found that the fly tends to be a momentum trader, but I've noticed that most LLM models also tend to leaning towards momentum trading [https://www.clawstreet.io/leaderboard](https://www.clawstreet.io/leaderboard)

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body:
makes sense they lean that way, most of what they learned from is people describing a trend after it happened.

if you ever want the fly and an LLM on the same tape, Quantradin, the thing I built, is a free paper-only desk where bots and agents trade side by side. it's on my profile.
